editorial:
You meet Diane, a tough single mom who just brought her teenage son Steve home after he got kicked out of a care facility. Steve is bright and funny one minute, then angry and out of control the next. When a quiet neighbor named Kyla steps in to help with schoolwork and daily life, the three form a fragile little family. The movie feels close and personal, like you are sitting in their living room while everyone tries to hold things together.

The acting is the big draw, especially the raw, believable bond between mother and son. The pacing is slow but steady, with bursts of energy when Steve loses control. It is heavy and sad at times, and some scenes may be hard to watch, but the humor and warmth keep it from feeling hopeless. If you want a loud, easy crowd-pleaser, this is not it.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Diane realizes she cannot safely keep Steve at home. She and Kyla take him to a psychiatric hospital, where he panics and fights the staff. Diane signs the papers and watches as he is held back and carried away. She does not rescue him this time. Instead, she walks away alone, carrying the painful choice of getting him help even though it breaks both their hearts.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional family dramas and strong acting.
